text:
maya: Quick sync — I'm putting together the rollout plan for fp8/4-bit across hosted endpoints. Need to lock down ops sanity heuristics and automatic fallback rules.

jeremy: +1. can we keep the initial canary tiny? 0.5-1% traffic.

sasha: agree on small canary. also: what are the exact quality metrics we gate on? degscore? ppl? task metrics?

luis: we should use a combo: deg_score for general safety, task-specific evals for critical endpoints (e.g. summarization rouge, qa exact match).

tara: ops constraints: must have an automated circuit-breaker that flips to int8/fp16 if deg_score delta > 0.06 over baseline for 5m window.

aditya: sounds good. also add a latency guard — if 95p latency increases by >30% we abort. some fp8 paths are slightly faster but some kernel combos regress.

maya: proposing default gate config (canary -> ramp -> global):
```
precision_gate:
  canary_pct: 1
  sample_size_per_min: 100
  deg_delta_threshold: 0.06
  fallback: int8
  fallback_grace_period: 10m
  latency_pct_increase_threshold: 0.3
```

jeremy: sample_size_per_min 100 might be low for low-signal endpoints. suggest also sample-based offline evals on the canary traffic (shadow compare).

sasha: +1. We should store prompt slices used for canary and run nightly replay tests against latest fp16/int8/fp8 to detect slow drifts.

luis: ops note — need a runtime flag to force-client-override for customers on Dedicated so they can opt-out of low-bit. Also require audit log entry on any automatic fallback.

maya: agreed. add config: customer_overrides: true & audit_log: true.

ops-bot: reminder: create a runbook entry before canary scheduling. Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/quant-rollouts

aditya: QA — we need an acceptance harness: 1k prompts per endpoint family, stratified by token length and domain. Run A/B diff on n-grams and hallucination heuristics. If any heuristics exceed thresholds -> block.

qa-bot: QA checklist created: https://redwood.internal/qa/lowbit-checklist (added sample generator + replay job).

maya: rollout cadence idea: canary 24h -> 5% for 48h -> 20% for 48h -> 100%. Each step requires health signals green for last 12h.

jeremy: add rollback criteria to PR template: if any customer-facing metric (NPS-ish) drops or support tickets spike >X in 1h, immediate rollback. Also tag SRE on-call.

luis: telemetry: we must surface per-model per-endpoint deg_delta, tokenwise rejection rate, latency P95/P99, cost delta. Dashboards + alerting.

maya: action items: 1) jeremy to draft circuit-breaker impl (runtime + API) 2) aditya + qa to finalize canary prompt sets 3) luis to add customer override + audit events 4) sasha to add nightly replay job 5) tara to add latency guard to autoscaler triggers

aditya: I'll take #2, aim to have sample sets in 48h.

jeremy: I'll prototype a small webhook that flips model variant and emits an event we can hook into alerting.

maya: one open question — acceptable deg_delta baseline numbers per workload. want ops + ML to propose defaults but allow endpoint overrides.

sasha: propose defaults: conversational (0.05), code-gen (0.04), summarization (0.07), retrieval-augmented QA (0.03). These are starting points, will tune with canary data.

luis: documenting this in the precision-runbook is critical. I'll add a section for per-workload defaults + how to request different thresholds for enterprise customers.

maya: perfect. I'll schedule a 30m follow-up tomorrow to sign off on runbook and gating configs. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
